title: Cache-access-pattern simulator and safe-config apply for prefix TTLs and key redesign
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reproducible simulator and safe-apply workflow for prefix K/V caching recommendations focused on hit-rate forecasting, TTL policy tuning, and cache-key redesign. The deliverable is a repeatable offline validation + staged rollout flow that produces a numeric hit-rate forecast and a safe apply policy (canary cohorts, rollback triggers, and post-apply verification). This ticket covers the simulator, config validators, CI checks, console UI hooks for recommended configs, and a small runtime safety-gate to auto-roll back if budgeted regressions are observed.
acceptance_criteria: Offline simulator can replay a 72-hour sampled production trace and output per-prefix hit-rate delta and cost delta for candidate TTL/key changes.
Simulator output includes uncertainty bounds (95% CI) and a recommended safety margin for staged applies.
A gated apply workflow is implemented: dry-run -> shadow -> 5% canary -> 25% -> global; each step has automated metric checks and rollback triggers.
Tech debt: all simulator code has unit tests and a documented evaluation notebook stored in Drive.
Console surfaces the top 10 TTL/key recommendations per tenant with expected token savings and the confidence score.
A runtime safety hook is deployed that will auto-rollback if hit-rate drops by >3% absolute or median request latency increases >15% within a 30-minute window.
PRs merged and an internal playbook added to the runbook library for intervention steps and postmortem templates.
decisions: Use a hybrid simulation approach: deterministic replay for observed traces plus bootstrapped resampling to estimate CI. This balances faithfulness to production and statistical confidence.
Estimate TTL impact by simulating prefix access inter-arrival times; candidate TTL is accepted only if simulated effective hit-rate improves without increasing tail latency in the model.
Cache-key redesign recommendations are limited to canonicalizations that are reversible and idempotent (no destructive key remapping) to simplify rollback.
Safety thresholds chosen conservatively (3% absolute hit-rate drop or 15% median tail latency) after reviewing historical incident sensitivity and business tolerance.
Do not auto-apply quantization or model-level changes in this ticket — focus on caching & keying only. Quantization belongs in a separate rollout pipeline.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Simulator: implement trace ingestion, prefix histogram builder, and IAT (inter-arrival time) sampler. Output: per-prefix baseline hit-rate and candidate hit-rate for TTL/key changes.
Phase 2 - Uncertainty & Scoring: add bootstrap resampling, compute 95% CI, and derive a confidence score + expected token cost delta per prefix.
Phase 3 - Validators & CI: static validators (no overlapping keys, canonicalization checksum), and a CI job that runs simulator on nightly sampled traces.
Phase 4 - Apply Workflow: implement dry-run and shadow deploy modes in the control plane; add canary filter criteria and enforcement hooks in the rollout service.
Phase 5 - Runtime Safety: runtime monitors that evaluate hit-rate, latency, and cost deltas; automatic rollback orchestration and alerting.
Phase 6 - Console & Docs: expose recommendations in Console, add links to evaluation notebook and playbook, and create a short runbook for on-call.
Phase 7 - Post-merge: run a 2-week internal beta with 3 tenants and iterate on thresholds and confidence scoring.
rollout_plan: Dry-run: run simulator and publish recommendations for review (no traffic changes).
Shadow deploy: route a copy of 5% of traffic through a cached variant to collect metric deltas without serving user-visible responses. Run for 24-72 hours.
Canary apply 1: apply config to 5% of traffic for 1 hour with real traffic and automated checks. If pass, proceed.
Canary apply 2: expand to 25% for 6 hours and evaluate again.
Global apply: expand to 100% during a low-traffic window; keep monitoring and enforce auto-rollback policy for 72 hours.
Fallback: for tenants with high sensitivity, require manual approval before canary.
test_plan: Unit tests: simulator components, validators, and scoring functions.
Integration tests: end-to-end replay against a synthetic trace that contains hot prefixes, cold prefixes, and bursty patterns.
Load tests: apply canary filters under 2x baseline QPS to ensure runtime safety hooks scale.
Chaos needle: simulate delayed cache invalidation and verify rollback path recovers within SLA window.
Continuous evaluation: nightly CI job that runs simulator on random 24h windows and checks for regressions in scoring logic.
metrics_to_monitor: Token cost per request and aggregate token spend delta
Error rate (5xx, 4xx increases correlated to rollout)
Rollout churn: number of auto-rollbacks and manual interventions
Confidence score and CI width for each recommended change
risks: Simulator mismatch: offline replay may not capture rare burst patterns leading to over-optimistic hit-rate estimates.
Key redesign edge cases: canonicalization could collate semantically distinct requests if not validated, causing correctness regressions.
Rollout flapping: aggressive auto-rollback could oscillate if thresholds are too tight under noisy metrics.
Tenant impact: misapplied TTLs could increase cold-miss cost for very latency-sensitive tenants.
mitigations: Use conservative confidence margins and require positive improvement across multiple windows before recommending global apply.
Keep cache-key changes reversible and add a small shadow test that compares outputs between legacy and new key paths before serving.
Implement hysteresis in rollback logic (require sustained violation for N datapoints) to avoid oscillation.
Expose an opt-out flag per-tenant and a review step for enterprise customers.
